guide.title: Discover the app
guide.description: Tap a feature to learn how to use it

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.desc: Overview with total balance, monthly income and expenses, evolution charts and category breakdown.
steps: Check your total balance at the top of the home page — it updates in real time as you add transactions.
Review this month's income and expenses with the colored KPI cards.
Explore the balance-evolution chart to follow your finances across recent months.
Inspect the category distribution donut to identify your biggest spending areas.
Use the Quick Preview button (or the Settings toggle) to see a splash overview before opening the full dashboard.
tips: The dashboard refreshes automatically after every new transaction.
Click any KPI card to drill into the matching transactions for the period.
Quick Preview on login is off by default — opt in from Settings → Preferences if you prefer the splash screen.

palette.title: Command Palette (⌘K)
palette.desc: Natural-language search that doubles as a calculator: find transactions, check budgets, list top expenses, compute averages — without leaving the keyboard.
steps: Open the palette with ⌘K / Ctrl+K, the sidebar Search button, or the Search tab in the mobile bottom nav.
Type free-form queries that mix type, category, period and merchant — e.g. "expenses loyer ytd", "uber may 2026", "easyjet april".
Run analytics with intent keywords: "budget shopping may 2026", "budget breaches", "top 10 ytd", "average expenses 2026".
Activate the pinned Result row to open a sheet with totals, category breakdown, progress bars (budget) or per-day averages (average).
Period chips show year-to-date by default — click the × on the chip to widen to all time.
tips: The parser is bilingual: "dépenses loyer cette année" and "expenses rent ytd" both work regardless of the UI language.
Recent queries are stored locally so re-running yesterday's search is one tap away.
Description tokens that don't match a category (e.g. "uber") fall back to free-text matching on transaction descriptions.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.desc: Manage every bank account, see individual balances and per-account transaction history.
steps: All your accounts appear on the Accounts page with their current balance.
Click an account to see its detail view with charts and full transaction history.
Add a new account anytime with the '+' button at the top of the page.
Edit name, bank or type from the account's three-dot menu.
Set custom aliases in Settings → Preferences for shorter labels in transfer descriptions.
tips: Each account's balance is recomputed automatically after every transaction touching it.
Use the Account Aliases section to shorten 'CB Gold' to 'SocGen' in transfer copy.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.desc: Record expenses, income and transfers. Link refunds, exclude one-offs from stats, search and filter the full history.
steps: Tap '+' to create a transaction; pick a type (expense, income or transfer between accounts).
Fill in amount, account, category and an optional description; for transfers, pick source and destination.
Link a refund to its original expense so the net figure stays accurate everywhere in the app.
Toggle "include in stats" off for one-offs you don't want skewing your KPIs.
Use the search bar and filter button on the Transactions page to narrow down quickly.
tips: For deeper queries, ⌘K / Search is faster than the filter panel — try "expenses Carrefour april".
Transfers between your own accounts don't change your total balance, only how it's distributed.
Partial refunds are supported: the original transaction tracks how much has been refunded so far.

budget.title: Budget
budget.desc: Set monthly budgets per category, track real vs. projected spend, and get notified when you're close or over.
steps: Open the Budget page from the sidebar to see real expenses, projected end-of-month spend and total budget side by side.
Set a monthly budget on a category from its detail view (or in bulk from the Budget page).
Visualise category share with the donut chart — hover a slice to see its value and percentage in the center.
Spot breaches faster from ⌘K: type "budget breaches" or "budget shopping may 2026" to get the same data inline.
Enable email budget alerts in Settings → Notifications to be warned when a category exceeds its limit.
tips: Cumulative-by-category chart shows whether you're tracking ahead or behind your budget mid-month.
Budgets are monthly — for a YTD query the app scales the budget by the number of months in the range.
A category with no budget set still appears in breakdowns; it just doesn't trigger alerts.

savings.title: Savings
savings.desc: Track savings derived from every transaction in an investment-type category, set goals and forecast progress.
steps: Any transaction (expense or income) tagged with an investment-type category counts toward Savings.
Review net savings, deposits, withdrawals and refunds from the Savings overview.
Create goals by giving them a name and target amount.
Track each goal's progress and the projected timeline (months remaining, monthly contribution needed).
tips: Set realistic goals using your average monthly savings — visible in the Reports page.
Income tagged as 'Investment' is a deposit; expense tagged as 'Investment' is a withdrawal.

debts.title: Debts
debts.desc: Track loans and credits with amortization schedules, principal/interest split, progress and automatic payments.
steps: Create a debt by setting type (loan given or received), total amount and interest rate.
Import a CSV schedule from your bank so each installment splits principal vs. interest correctly.
Enable automatic recurring payments so every installment is recorded without manual work.
Follow progress in real time: amount paid, remaining, completion bar and full payment history.
Open a debt's detail to see the full schedule and breakdown.
tips: The CSV importer auto-detects your bank's format (separator, date layout, decimal style).
Overdue installments appear in red in the scheduled calendar so you can act before they pile up.
Each debt payment is linked to its transaction — editing or deleting one updates the other.

recurring.title: Recurring
recurring.desc: Schedule repeat expenses and income (rent, salary, subscriptions). Visual calendar and automatic processing.
steps: Add a recurring transaction with amount, frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly) and account.
View all upcoming occurrences in the calendar — click a day to see what's scheduled.
Automatic processing creates the transaction on its due date; past occurrences run on next launch.
Run an occurrence ahead of schedule from the card, or pause it without deleting.
Debts and installments create linked recurring entries automatically.
tips: Overdue debt installments show in red in the calendar for immediate visibility.
The '7 days' badge at the top of the page warns you of upcoming charges this week.
Switch between Calendar and List views depending on whether you want timing or detail.

installments.title: Installments
installments.desc: Track buy-now-pay-later purchases and incoming repayments with progress bars, history and automatic recurring transactions.
steps: Create an installment plan with total amount, monthly amount, frequency and start date.
Pick the direction: payment (you pay) or reimbursement (you receive).
An automatic recurring transaction is created and linked to the plan.
Follow progress via the completion bar, paid amount and remaining amount.
Adjust the plan mid-stream: change monthly amount or remaining installment count.
tips: The ⋯ menu on each card opens details, history and a recalc-plan option.
History shows each installment with status (paid, upcoming) and a link to its transaction.
Once all installments are paid the plan auto-flips to completed status.

reports.title: Analysis
reports.desc: Deep dive into your finances: balance evolution, category breakdowns, recurring spend, income sources and exportable reports.
steps: Open the Analysis page from the sidebar (also accessible via 'reports' in ⌘K).
Pick a period — 1 month, 3 months, year to date, 1 year or a custom range.
Explore the tabs: Evolution, Categories, Recurring, Income — each with its own visual.
Hover the category donut to inspect a slice's amount and share without losing the total.
Export reports as PDF or Excel from the export menu, or build a custom report with the wizard.
tips: Compare two periods month-over-month to spot the trend behind a sudden total change.
The cumulative-by-category chart pairs nicely with the Budget page for mid-month sanity checks.

notifications.title: Email notifications
notifications.desc: Receive budget breach alerts and a monthly financial report by email.
steps: Enable notifications in Settings → Notifications.
Turn on Budget alerts to get an email when a category exceeds its monthly cap.
Turn on Monthly reports to receive a complete financial summary at the start of each month.
The monthly report includes a PDF with income, expenses, category breakdown and trend.
tips: Budget alerts are sent at most once per category per month to avoid spam.
The monthly report compares with the previous month so trends are obvious.
Set category budgets first — alerts depend on them existing.

privacy.title: Privacy & device
privacy.desc: Control what's visible on screen, install the app on this device and watch the sync state.
steps: Toggle Privacy mode in Settings → Privacy & data to blur amounts and balances on screen.
Export your transactions as CSV from the same panel.
Request account deletion from the destructive action there (routes through support email).
Install Spending Tracker as a PWA from Settings → Device & sync for offline-capable, full-screen access.
Live sync status (online / offline / queued changes) is also surfaced in Device & sync.
tips: Privacy mode is great in public — toggle from the sidebar icon for quick access.
Once installed as a PWA the app keeps working offline and queues changes for next sync.
Settings is reactive: any preference change propagates instantly across the app, no reload needed.

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Customize the app: profile, currency, date format, accounts, categories, notifications, privacy, device and locale.
steps: Navigate via the left rail (desktop) or the horizontal section strip (mobile) to jump between Profile, Preferences, Notifications, Accounts, Privacy & data, Device & sync, Guide and Sign out.
In Preferences: pick currency, date format, calculation date (accounting vs. value), language, and the optional Quick Preview-on-login splash.
In Privacy & data: privacy mode toggle, CSV export and account deletion request.
In Device & sync: PWA install entry point and live sync state.
Revisit this guide anytime from Settings → Guide.
tips: Setting a value date instead of accounting date changes how charts and KPIs split transactions across months.
Account Aliases shorten transfer descriptions ('CB Gold' → 'SocGen') across the entire app.
